name: English nationalism
summary: English nationalism holds that the English are a nation entitled to political recognition and self-government, usually through an English parliament in a federal UK or, for some, an independent England. Its organised forms are Eurosceptic and favour sovereignty, tighter immigration and citizenship rules, and protection of English culture and history, with a mostly mixed-economy, right-of-centre outlook. Adherents differ on whether the English nation is civic or ethnic.
scope: Contemporary political English nationalism as set out in the English Democrats' manifesto (an English parliament, leaving the EU, ending mass immigration) and the Campaign for an English Parliament's constitutional case (equal devolution, civic nation, fairer funding). Excludes cultural Englishness without a political programme, British nationalism, and street-level movements such as the English Defence League. Most economic and social questions are not addressed by these sources, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The English Democrats want an NHS giving a high-quality service for all citizens, so tax-funded universal care is accepted, though restricted to citizens.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The manifesto says a healthy economy is a mixed economy and wants less reliance on the City, so neither side of this claim is endorsed outright.

public-ownership.rationale: The sources are silent on nationalising utilities; the party's mixed-economy stance leaves adherents split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The manifesto wants fairer trade and less City dominance but gives no general stance on corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The manifesto would cap welfare payments for larger families, a sign of welfare scepticism, but wholesale cuts are not demanded.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The CEP complains of political correctness and revisionism and the English Democrats list it as a key grievance, so speech restrictions are disliked.

strong-leader.rationale: The manifesto stresses law above all including the monarch and referenda on constitutional change, pointing against bypassing parliament.

decide-locally.rationale: The CEP opposes regional assemblies and defends shire local government, but wants an English-level parliament; this is split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The manifesto mentions the Christian community only in a list of groups the law should treat even-handedly.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The English Democrats' manifesto aims to preserve and build on English cultural unity, and the CEP seeks protection of English culture and history.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement seeks constitutional reform through referenda and Parliament and is associated with conservative values, not revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The manifesto calls for a points system to end mass immigration, border controls and deportation of illegal immigrants.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party refuses deals that undermine English sovereignty and would leave the 1951 Refugee Convention.

free-trade.rationale: The manifesto backs fair trade and reciprocity ('fairs fair') rather than unconditional free trade and wants more manufacturing.

nation-first.rationale: England's independence and sovereignty are placed above supranational commitments in the manifesto.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The manifesto backs NATO only as a strictly defensive alliance, implying wariness of interventions abroad.

open-borders.rationale: The manifesto seeks to end mass immigration and tighten border controls.

limit-growth.rationale: The manifesto wants more manufacturing and growth; degrowth is not an English nationalist theme.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement works through referenda, parliament and elections and stresses the rule of law.

central-planning.rationale: The manifesto explicitly supports a mixed economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The manifesto wants more manufacturing and less City reliance, hinting at some state role, but no programme is given.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The manifesto's mixed economy and living wage assume money and wage labour continue.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The manifesto offers no state-recognised wage bodies and prefers a living wage set by law.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement contests elections and the manifesto favours referenda and proportional representation for English elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The manifesto says the law is above all including the monarch, accepting the monarchy rather than abolishing it; no republican plank exists.

democracy-best.rationale: The manifesto commits to referenda, an elected English parliament and electoral reform.

direct-votes.rationale: The manifesto wants constitutional changes referred to the electorate in referenda.

workers-councils.rationale: The programme is a parliamentary one centred on an English parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: The English Democrats at one stage sought an independent England outside the UK, assuming a right of nations to self-rule.

natural-rulers.rationale: The manifesto rests on equality before the law and democratic accountability.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement is electoral and the manifesto stresses rule of law, though no pacifist statement appears.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Church of England is part of English tradition; the manifesto does not propose separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The manifesto proposes a secular legal order under a Bill of Rights of English liberties and the law above all.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The manifesto calls for democratically accountable police and a state defence policy.

military-superiority.rationale: The manifesto keeps a deterrent and NATO but frames defence as defensive, with no rivalry doctrine.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The CEP explicitly embraces a civic not ethnic conception of the English nation; the English Democrats are accused of ethnic leanings, so the mainstream is split but leans civic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: No Marxist analysis; the manifesto speaks of an English community accommodating all.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal treatment before the law, not equal outcomes.

civilizational-union.rationale: The manifesto stresses independent English sovereignty over wider unions.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The manifesto proposes a Bill of Rights of traditional English liberties, but also communal belonging; not clearly either.

limit-population.rationale: The manifesto addresses numbers through immigration control rather than population policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The manifesto wants more manufacturing and no anti-industrial theme appears.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Associated with conservative values that favour inherited institutions over disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The manifesto stresses democratic accountability and referenda, against technocratic delegation.

restore-past-order.rationale: The CEP appeals to a legacy built by ancestors, but its aim is a modern parliament; adherents are split between restorers and reformers.

direct-action.rationale: The movement uses elections and lobbying, with the manifesto stressing referenda and law.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The manifesto wants more manufacturing; no primitivist content.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of a programme that retains a mixed economy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The manifesto stresses reciprocity and fair trade and restricts the NHS and welfare to citizens, not need regardless of work.

production-for-use.rationale: The manifesto accepts a mixed economy with markets.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programme backs a mixed economy and no Marxist theory of exploitation appears.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The movement is parliamentary and democratic.

collective-farming.rationale: Not part of a mixed-economy programme.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: No such analysis appears; defence policy is NATO-based.

taxation-theft.rationale: The manifesto calls for honest taxation and an English parliament with tax powers, not abolition.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement is a group-rights claim for the English as a nation, though it also favours a Bill of Rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The manifesto stresses voting, referenda and an elected parliament.

media-academia-power.rationale: The CEP blames academics, media and politicians for revisionism, and the English Democrats list political correctness as a key issue.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The CEP describes a civic nation regardless of ethnicity and the party rejects accusations of racism; hereditarian claims are not part of the programme.

organic-representation.rationale: The manifesto proposes a conventional parliament, with proportional representation for English elections.

total-state.rationale: The manifesto favours a mixed economy and traditional English civil liberties.

national-rebirth.rationale: The CEP speaks of a nation weakened by seventy years of failed policy needing its own voice, but not of radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The manifesto favours a strictly defensive NATO and an independent England; no expansionism is stated.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The manifesto stresses the rule of law above all.

bound-labor.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal legal treatment of citizens.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The CEP complaint about revisionism presumes an objectively correct history.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The manifesto does not propose worker voice in company management.

school-vouchers.rationale: The manifesto supports parental choice in education but does not mention vouchers.

rule-by-example.rationale: The manifesto stresses law above all and a Bill of Rights.

national-self-determination.rationale: The CEP and English Democrats' core claim is that England is a nation entitled to its own parliament, and independence in the English Democrats' earlier platform.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The manifesto says NHS services should not be freely available to non-nationals and wants welfare restricted.

class-collaboration.rationale: The manifesto aims for a society accommodating all English people, without class struggle language.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The CEP wants English culture and history protected from revisionism and the manifesto aims to preserve cultural unity.

dominated-front.rationale: The manifesto backs NATO and ties with like-minded states.

workers-nation.rationale: English nationalism is linked with working-class English identity, with class and nation intersecting.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal treatment of all citizens before the law.

ban-interest.rationale: The manifesto accepts a mixed market economy with finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The manifesto stresses all citizens treated equally before the law and rejects racism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: No class theory of the state; the manifesto aims at a society serving all people of England.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The manifesto wants to extend territorial waters but gives no energy policy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The manifesto speaks of preserving English cultural unity and of English identity as community membership.

elite-replacement.rationale: Mainstream bodies like the CEP and the party reject racism accusations; a replacement conspiracy is a fringe addition.

proportional-representation.rationale: The manifesto favours reforming the voting system for English elections toward proportional representation.

national-mission.rationale: The manifesto's defence is strictly defensive and focused on England.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The CEP blames Westminster for failed policy and lavish spending and the party stresses honest taxation and accountable police.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal rights before the law; eugenics is not part of it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The manifesto wants police to be democratically accountable but does not speak of past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The manifesto supports an NHS, education, welfare and a mixed economy, beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The CEP's civic conception and the party's rejection of racism contradict this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal treatment of all citizens under the law, though its welfare and healthcare rules differ for non-nationals.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: English nationalists see the English as an indigenous nation, not a settler colonial one.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The manifesto stresses the law is above all and equal treatment of all communities.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The manifesto does not restrict religion and lists religious communities among groups the law should treat equally.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No such concept; not part of English nationalism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The manifesto's referenda and elected English parliament assume authority rests on voters.

population-transfer.rationale: The manifesto proposes deporting illegal immigrants, but not forced removal of minorities; mainstream bodies deny racism.

separated-powers.rationale: The manifesto favours a Bill of Rights and law above all including the monarch, implying checks on power.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement is parliamentary and democratic.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The manifesto aims for a society accommodating all English people but does not prioritise the poor.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The manifesto links numbers to immigration rather than poverty causation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The manifesto favours elections and a parliament.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The manifesto's Bill of Rights stresses traditional English civil liberties and the law above all.

party-controls-media.rationale: The manifesto asks for far-ranging freedom of access to information.

party-commands-army.rationale: The manifesto contains no such proposal and stresses the law above all.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The manifesto would raise the residency requirement for citizenship to a minimum of 10 years.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The manifesto will not support deals that undermine England's sovereignty and the party endorsed Brexit.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The manifesto stresses the law above all including the monarch and an elected parliament.

clerical-rule.rationale: The manifesto is secular and parliamentary.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The manifesto supports NATO and defence.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The manifesto favours freedom of access to information and opposes political correctness.

recall-officials.rationale: The manifesto stresses democratic accountability and referenda, so recall is a consistent but unstated inference.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The manifesto supports NATO as a strictly defensive alliance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not part of a mixed-economy programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: The manifesto keeps a state military and nuclear deterrent.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The CEP defends shire local government and traditional counties, but no rural moral claim is stated.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The English Democrats call for a Monmouthshire referendum on joining England, a minor border claim, but nothing like reunification.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The CEP calls England a nation that built something envied by the world, a stance not neutral between cultures.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The manifesto wants quality education equal across England; no creationism plank.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The manifesto lengthens naturalisation but ties identity to community not blood; the CEP rejects an ethnic conception.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The manifesto stresses the law above all and equal treatment, not exemptions.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The English Democrats' independence goal is constitutional, with no demand for economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The manifesto wants referenda on constitutional change and an English parliament within existing structures, not a new assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The manifesto stresses traditional English civil liberties and a Bill of Rights.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The manifesto stresses England-first policy and fair trade, not aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The manifesto says England should retain a nuclear deterrent.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The manifesto accepts the monarch as head of state under the law and proposes no presidential election.

collective-defense.rationale: The manifesto supports NATO as a strictly defensive alliance, which rests on mutual defence.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The manifesto keeps the monarchy under the law, and the monarch is by convention above party politics.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The manifesto places even the monarch beneath the law.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The manifesto calls for honest taxation but gives no rate structure.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The manifesto states that the law is above all, including the monarch.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement is parliamentary and the manifesto subordinates all, including the monarch, to law.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not relevant to a non-socialist movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not part of a mixed-economy programme that respects property.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The English Democrats' Monmouthshire referendum call is a border adjustment, not a claim based on nationality; the manifesto otherwise targets England only.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The manifesto is secular and stresses civil liberties.

women-must-cover.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal treatment and traditional English civil liberties.

common-currency.rationale: The manifesto rejects deals undermining English sovereignty and the party backed leaving the EU.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The manifesto stresses England's independence; a wider union of peoples is not proposed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The manifesto wants unified English cultural identity and treating all citizens equally in law.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement emphasises culture, identity and constitutional grievance, not economic determinism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The manifesto wants referenda but also a Bill of Rights that restrains government; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The manifesto asks for equal treatment of citizens, not quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The manifesto supports fair trade links with like-minded states rather than a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The manifesto wants reciprocal trade ('fairs fair') but names no labour or environmental standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: The manifesto keeps a mixed market economy with wages.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The manifesto accepts the monarchy and proposes a reformed second chamber without calling for abolition of titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The CEP wants English history defended from revisionism and English culture protected, which supports teaching history centred on England.

patriotic-education.rationale: The manifesto calls for compulsory flying of the English flag on state buildings and cultural unity, implying pride in the nation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The manifesto backs a mixed economy and has no collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The manifesto concentrates on England and rejects supranational entanglement.

delink-world-market.rationale: The manifesto seeks fair trade links with like-minded states.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The manifesto asks that all citizens be treated equally; absolute private freedom to discriminate is not part of the programme.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The manifesto calls for a Bill of Rights founded on traditional English civil liberties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The manifesto accepts a hereditary monarch under the law.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The manifesto places the monarch under the law but proposes no right of resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The manifesto states that the law is above all, including the monarch, and seeks an English Parliament and Prime Minister.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is a political one that asks people to join and campaign.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The CEP says media and academics revise English history, but does not claim mass culture pacifies people.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No such theory appears in the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: The manifesto raises citizenship residency to 10 years but does not address reserving posts to the native born.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The manifesto does not address this and speaks of equal treatment of citizens.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The manifesto states that the law is above all and puts police and forces under democratic accountability.

office-by-exam.rationale: The manifesto favours elected bodies and referenda over examination-based rule.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The manifesto wants more manufacturing and less reliance on the City but no specific takeover rule.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The mixed economy and property respect run against communal land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The manifesto places parliament and law above the crown and seeks an English parliament; budget control follows from parliamentary supremacy.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The manifesto insists on equal treatment, not equal outcome tests.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The manifesto frames defence as strictly defensive.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The manifesto stresses national independence and defensive military posture.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The manifesto caps welfare for larger families, which cuts against financial incentives for births.

job-guarantee.rationale: The manifesto does not propose employer-of-last-resort schemes.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The manifesto places the law above all.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream bodies reject racism accusations; a conspiracy claim is a fringe element.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The manifesto offers nothing of the kind and is socially conservative in tone.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The manifesto asks for far-ranging freedom of access to information.

local-production.rationale: The manifesto wants more manufacturing but does not tie production to place.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is organised as parties and campaign groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The manifesto would withdraw from the 1951 Refugee Convention and rejects deals undermining English sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: The manifesto speaks of an English community open to all, with Christian community only listed among groups.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The CEP wants the Barnett formula scrapped and money raised in England spent in England.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The mixed economy assumes private possessions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The manifesto backs parental choice in education but nothing on provider mix.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The manifesto asks for equal treatment, not economic transformation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The manifesto backs a mixed economy, which can be read as a middle path.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Monmouthshire referendum idea has a historical element but no general principle is stated.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream English nationalist bodies reject accusations of racism and extremism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal treatment and traditional English civil liberties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The manifesto asks for civil liberties and freedom of information.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The manifesto offers no blasphemy law and stresses civil liberties.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The manifesto is domestic and independence-focused.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The CEP rejects what it sees as revisionist academic currents.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement is described as right-of-centre, but the CEP is cross-party.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The manifesto's referenda and parliament place authority in the electorate.

social-market-economy.rationale: The manifesto combines a mixed economy with an NHS, welfare and fair trade, close to this model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The manifesto retains a nuclear deterrent and NATO membership.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a constitutional or ceremonial crown, and the statement now asks only about passing real governing power to a child.

reviewHistory.rationale: The manifesto accepts the monarchy, which is hereditary.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a constitutional or ceremonial crown, and the statement now asks only about passing real governing power to a child.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The manifesto accepts a market economy with finance.

property-franchise.rationale: The manifesto proposes referenda and an elected English parliament on equal terms.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The manifesto puts law above all including the monarch and wants a Bill of Rights.

racial-franchise.rationale: The CEP defines the nation civically, representing anyone legitimately living in England regardless of ethnicity.

open-government-data.rationale: The manifesto asks for far-ranging freedom of access to information.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The manifesto lists religions among groups the law should treat equally.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The manifesto requires equal treatment of all citizens.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The manifesto wants less City reliance but makes no liberty claim about wealth.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The manifesto is not hostile to religion and lists Christian communities among those treated equally.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The manifesto proposes democratically accountable police.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The manifesto backs an NHS and welfare while capping benefits, so it is mixed.

vote-delegation.rationale: The manifesto proposes ordinary referenda and parliaments.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The manifesto stresses equal treatment of citizens; shared authority is an inference.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement demands a state of its own, an English parliament and accountable police, so it values the state as an instrument of national self-rule.

culture-before-state.rationale: The defining demand is a state institution, an English parliament, which is pursued as a political project ahead of any cultural revival.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The CEP conceives the English nation as civic and cross-party, so economic life is not reserved for a majority group, though some ethnic-nationalist adherents differ.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The CEP opposes regional assemblies and wants England as a whole to have one parliament like Scotland's, which merges its regions into a single unit.

municipal-property.rationale: A right-of-centre mixed economy has no place for community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement wants a single English parliament and national sovereignty rather than confederations of towns.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Campaign for an English Parliament defines the English nation as civic and open to all residents, so organising by racial interests is rejected by the mainstream, though an ethnic strand differs.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in English history and culture is central; the ethnic strand frames this as ancestry and the civic strand as national pride.

communal-electorates.rationale: The English Democrats and the CEP want one equal citizenship and a common English parliament, with no separate religious electorates.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Campaign for an English Parliament seeks constitutional change through Parliament and equal devolution, within existing institutions.

sacred-nation.rationale: The CEP's case defends English history and culture and treats the English as a nation with lasting claims, though in a civic rather than religious register.

internal-colonialism.rationale: English nationalists argue England is disadvantaged by the Barnett formula and Westminster, the opposite direction of a wealthy centre exploiting poor regions within England.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Its core demand is an English parliament, a representative institution, and it campaigns through party and pressure group.

national-resource-control.rationale: Its Eurosceptic case rests on national sovereignty, including control of England's own affairs and resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Nothing in the English Democrats or CEP material addresses distributive justice; adherents' mixed-economy right-of-centre outlook gives no clear lean either way.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The English Democrats and CEP are multi-party, democratic and mixed-economy; a communist-party-led system is the opposite of their civic-constitutional programme.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The manifesto would cap welfare payments for larger families, a sign of welfare scepticism, but wholesale cuts are not demanded. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: England should have its own parliament with the same powers over domestic affairs as Scotland's.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining demand of both the English Democrats and the Campaign for an English Parliament, answering devolution inequality.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to UK devolution; decide-locally and region-keeps-system cover the general question.

missingStatements.text: Tax raised in one part of a country should mainly be spent in that part rather than shared by a funding formula.
missingStatements.rationale: The CEP wants the Barnett formula scrapped and English taxes spent for the benefit of those who earn them.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Barnett formula; not a general question across ideologies.

notes: The English Democrats were described as far-right by critics and the CEP stresses a civic conception; the two disagree on ethnicity-linked questions. Many answers are inferred from a thin policy record.
